title: Family Rights Violations — Parental Alienation, Hague Convention 1980, and UN Convention on the Rights of the Child Violations Resulting from Aviation Incidents
category: International Aviation / Human Rights / Treaty Law
allegation_summary: The LA8159 and GRU aviation incidents were exploited to interfere with the passenger's parental relationship with his daughter. The lifetime ban imposed by LATAM without evidence prevented the passenger from traveling to Santiago to exercise visitation and parental rights. This created a de facto parental alienation situation where aviation security measures were weaponized to separate a father from his child after the incident. The passenger's daughter, a minor and Italian/Brazilian citizen, was deprived of contact with her father. No claim is made that the child was physically present at the airport removal scene; the claim concerns post-incident separation impact. These actions violate multiple international instruments protecting family unity and children's rights, including: the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) Articles 3, 9, 10, and 11; the Hague Convention of 25 October 1980 on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction; and the American Convention on Human Rights Articles 17 (Family) and 19 (Rights of the Child).
